title: The Pleasures of the Damned

vibeProfile.oneLine: A career-spanning best-of Bukowski's plainspoken poetry.

summary: A generous posthumous selection of Bukowski's poems spanning his whole career, from the early barroom pieces to the wry, softened reflections on death of his final years. Chosen as a career-spanning introduction, it shows the surprising range beneath the tough-guy reputation: humour, grief, tenderness and a hard-won clarity about living and dying. For anyone wanting one Bukowski poetry book, this is the place to start.
whyReadIt: The one-volume best of Bukowski's poetry, career-spanning and surprisingly tender. The place to start.

funFacts.text: Published after his death, it collects poems from across his four decades of writing.
